data.gender_notes: Bhavanee is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhavanee is a Hindu name for Goddess Saraswati, the deity of knowledge, music, art, wisdom, and nature. It also refers to the creator of the universe. The name Bhavanee carries the meaning “Goddess of Creation” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhavanee usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of creation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: One who embodies wisdom and creativity.
data.etymology: Bhavanee belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Creation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhavanee total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

Goddess Bhavani, as the embodiment of the divine power, is believed to grant wisdom, knowledge, and inspiration to seekers. The name Bhavanee is often invoked during spiritual practices and rituals, and is an integral part of Hindu spirituality, art, and literature.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Bhavanee represents the divine inner teacher and guide, bestowing the seeker with deep internal knowledge and wisdom. The name evokes a sense of reverence, devotion, and connection to the divine, encouraging one to embark on a spiritual journey towards self-realization and enlightenment. Bhavanee symbolizes the creative power of the universe, inspiring us to tap into our potential for growth and transformation. Ultimately, the name Bhavanee serves as a reminder of the divine presence within us, guiding us towards a deeper understanding of ourselves and the world around us.

vedic_reference.note: Not directly from Vedas, but from later Hindu literature and mythology

historical_references.reference: Bhavani is an aspect of Parvati, the consort of Shiva. She is known as the goddess of wisdom, power, and motherly love. The name Bhavani is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Bhava', which means 'existence' or 'manifestation'.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient Hindu texts, likely originating from 2nd millennium BCE or earlier

historical_references.reference: In the Puranic literature, Bhavani is mentioned as the mother of the god Ganesha. She is also known as Ganesha's adoptive mother, as Parvati gave him life by breathing the divine essence into the clay statue which her husband Shiva had shaped.
historical_references.time_period: Puranic texts, likely originating from 4th to 8th centuries CE
